words.zhGloss: 你的声音听起来闷闷的
words.enDefinition: Used to tell someone that their voice sounds covered or less clear than usual.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你的声音听起来闷闷的

examples.en: Your voice sounds muffled over the phone, especially when you turn away from it.
examples.zh: 电话里「你的声音听起来闷闷的」，特别是你转身背对手机的时候。

examples.en: Your voice sounds muffled through the door, so let me know when you're inside.
examples.zh: 隔着门「你的声音听起来闷闷的」，你进来后跟我说一声吧。

collocations: your voice sounds muffled over the phone
tell them your voice sounds muffled
your voice sounds muffled through the door

words.enDefinition: A polite request for someone to repeat what they just said.

examples.en: Could you say that again after this bus passes so everyone can hear the instructions?
examples.zh: 等这辆公交车过去后，「你能再说一遍吗」？这样大家都能听清指引。

examples.en: Could you say that again for the two people sorting boxes outside the kitchen?
examples.zh: 「你能再说一遍吗」？厨房外面还有两个人在整理箱子。

collocations: could you say that again more slowly
could you say that again for everyone
could you say that again from the start

words.enDefinition: A question checking whether a word or name is written with a hyphen.

examples.en: Is there a hyphen between the two words on the name tag you ordered?
examples.zh: 你订的名牌上，两个词「中间有连字符吗」？

examples.en: Is there a hyphen in the street name, or do I write it as one word?
examples.zh: 街道名里「有连字符吗」，还是应该连起来写成一个词？

collocations: is there a hyphen between the words
is there a hyphen in the name
ask is there a hyphen

words.enDefinition: A request for someone to speak more loudly because they are difficult to hear.

examples.en: Could you speak up a little because the fans at the back are very loud?
examples.zh: 后面的风扇很吵，「你能说大声一点吗」？

examples.en: Could you speak up so my friend at the end of the table can hear?
examples.zh: 「你能说大声一点吗」？这样坐在桌子另一头的朋友也能听见。

collocations: could you speak up a little
could you speak up over the noise
could you speak up so everyone can hear

words.enDefinition: Used to tell someone that very little of what they are saying is audible.

examples.en: I can hardly hear you over the crowd near the entrance to the concert hall.
examples.zh: 音乐厅入口附近的人群太吵，「我几乎听不见你说话」。

examples.en: I can hardly hear you on speaker, so let's move away from the open window.
examples.zh: 开着免提时「我几乎听不见你说话」，我们离开这扇开着的窗户吧。

collocations: I can hardly hear you over the music
I can hardly hear you from here
I can hardly hear you on speaker

words.enDefinition: Used to explain that audio reaches the listener noticeably later than expected.

examples.en: The sound is delayed on my side, so I may answer a little late.
examples.zh: 我这里「声音有延迟」，所以我可能会晚一点回答。

examples.en: The sound is delayed on this call even though the picture is perfectly clear.
examples.zh: 这通电话里「声音有延迟」，画面倒是很清楚。

collocations: the sound is delayed on my side
notice the sound is delayed
say the sound is delayed

words.zhGloss: 我们能换个安静一点的地方吗
words.enDefinition: A request to continue a conversation somewhere with less noise so people can hear.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们能换个安静一点的地方吗

examples.en: Can we move somewhere quieter so I can hear the instructions for tomorrow morning?
examples.zh: 「我们能换个安静一点的地方吗」？我想听清明天上午的安排。

examples.en: Can we move somewhere quieter to talk where the sound of the fan won't distract us?
examples.zh: 「我们能换个安静一点的地方吗」？免得说话时一直被风扇声打扰。

collocations: can we move somewhere quieter to talk
can we move somewhere quieter for this call
ask can we move somewhere quieter

words.enDefinition: Used before saying the only part of a message you were able to hear.

examples.en: All I heard was the word Friday before the loudspeaker cut off in the hallway.
examples.zh: 走廊的扬声器没声以前，「我只听到了」星期五这个词。

examples.en: All I heard was the room number, so I still need to know the building.
examples.zh: 「我只听到了」房间号，所以还得知道是哪一栋楼。

collocations: all I heard was the start
all I heard was the word Tuesday
all I heard was the end

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to repeat the ending of what they just said.

examples.en: What was the last part of the address you gave me for the rehearsal tonight?
examples.zh: 你刚给了我今晚排练的地址，「最后那部分是什么」？

examples.en: What was the last part again before everyone started talking at the same time?
examples.zh: 大家一起开口之前那句，「最后那部分是什么」来着？

collocations: what was the last part of that
what was the last part again
ask what was the last part

words.enDefinition: From the beginning of something such as a set of directions, a text, or a rehearsal.

examples.en: Can we take it from the top so I can note each change in order?
examples.zh: 我们能「从头开始」吗？我想按顺序记下每处改动。

examples.en: Let's go through it from the top now that everyone can hear us clearly.
examples.zh: 现在大家都能听清我们说话了，我们「从头开始」过一遍吧。

collocations: take it from the top
start from the top
go through it from the top

words.enDefinition: Separately, saying or dealing with each word before moving on to the next one.

examples.en: Please say it one word at a time while I type the street name into the app.
examples.zh: 我把街道名输进应用时，请「一个词一个词地说」。

examples.en: She read the address one word at a time because our phone connection was weak.
examples.zh: 我们的电话信号弱，所以她「一个词一个词地」念地址。

collocations: say it one word at a time
read it one word at a time
repeat it one word at a time

words.enDefinition: Used to identify the words you believe you heard so the other person can confirm them.

examples.en: I heard you say half past two, but the sign says the tour starts at three.
examples.zh: 「我听见你说了」两点半，但牌子上写着导览三点开始。

examples.en: I heard you say something about the back door before the driver made an announcement.
examples.zh: 司机广播之前，「我听见你说了」些关于后门的事。

collocations: I heard you say the time
I heard you say Friday
I heard you say something about the bus

words.enDefinition: Used to report an uncertain impression of what words someone said.

examples.en: It sounded like you said fifteen minutes, but I couldn't tell over the announcement.
examples.zh: 「听起来你像是在说」十五分钟，但广播太响，我不敢确定。

examples.en: It sounded like you said north gate, so I wanted to check before we started walking.
examples.zh: 「听起来你像是在说」北门，所以出发走过去之前我想确认一下。

collocations: it sounded like you said Tuesday
it sounded like you said the other entrance
it sounded like you said something else

words.expression: I can't make out the words
words.lemma: i can't make out the words
words.zhGloss: 我分辨不出说的是什么
words.enDefinition: Used to say you can hear someone speaking but cannot distinguish the individual words.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我分辨不出说的是什么
acceptedEnVariants: I can't make out the words

examples.en: I can't make out the words from here, but I think that's our platform announcement.
examples.zh: 从这儿「我分辨不出说的是什么」，但我觉得是关于我们站台的广播。

examples.en: I can't make out the words on the recording after the sound of the door closing.
examples.zh: 录音传来关门声后，「我分辨不出说的是什么」。

collocations: I can't make out the words over the noise
I can't make out the words from here
I can't make out the words on the recording

words.enDefinition: Used when you realise you heard different words from the ones someone actually said.

examples.en: I misheard you and wrote down room forty instead of room fourteen on the notice.
examples.zh: 「我听错了你的话」，在通知上写成了四十号房，实际是十四号。

examples.en: I think I misheard you when you said how far the station was from here.
examples.zh: 你说车站离这里多远时，我想「我听错了你的话」。

collocations: I think I misheard you
I misheard you the first time
I misheard you over the noise

words.zhGloss: 被别的声音盖住而听不清
words.enDefinition: Used to describe speech or other audio which another sound makes hard to hear.
acceptedZhAnswers: 被别的声音盖住而听不清

examples.en: The announcement was hard to hear over the engines of the buses outside the terminal.
examples.zh: 车站外的公交车引擎声太响，「盖住了广播，听不清」。

examples.en: Your directions were hard to hear over the music coming from the other end of the hall.
examples.zh: 大厅另一头的音乐声「盖过了你说的路线，我听不清」。

collocations: hard to hear over the music
hard to hear over traffic
hard to hear over the engines

words.zhGloss: 你能逐个字母拼出来吗
words.enDefinition: asks someone to say the letters of a word or name one by one
acceptedZhAnswers: 你能逐个字母拼出来吗
你能把字母一个个拼出来吗

examples.en: Could you spell it out for me so I don't send the card to the wrong street?
examples.zh: 「你能逐个字母拼出来吗」？我不想把卡片寄到错误的街道。

examples.en: Could you spell it out slowly while I type the name into the visitor list?
examples.zh: 我把名字输进访客名单，你能「慢慢逐个字母拼出来」吗？

collocations: could you spell it out for me
could you spell it out slowly
could you spell it out over the phone

words.expression: is that one word or two
words.lemma: is that one word or two
words.zhGloss: 那是一个词还是两个词
words.enDefinition: A question asking whether something should be written together or with a space.
acceptedZhAnswers: 那是一个词还是两个词
acceptedEnVariants: is that one word or two

examples.en: Is that one word or two when I write the club name on the sign?
examples.zh: 我把俱乐部名写到指示牌上时，「那是一个词还是两个词」？

examples.en: Is that one word or two in the name of the meeting room upstairs?
examples.zh: 楼上会议室的名字里，「那是一个词还是两个词」？

collocations: is that one word or two on the label
is that one word or two in writing
ask is that one word or two

words.enDefinition: A question asking whether a letter in a word or name should be uppercase.

examples.en: Is that with a capital M when I write the name on the envelope?
examples.zh: 我在信封上写名字时，「M 要用大写吗」？

examples.en: Is that with a capital at the start, or should I copy the lowercase version?
examples.zh: 「那里要用大写字母开头吗」，还是我照抄小写的版本？

collocations: is that with a capital at the start
is that with a capital M
ask is that with a capital

words.enDefinition: An example used to identify the letter A clearly by saying a familiar word beginning with it.

examples.en: I said “A as in apple” because the receptionist thought the first letter was E.
examples.zh: 接待员以为第一个字母是 E，我就说「A，apple 的首字母」。

examples.en: Could you confirm “A as in apple” for the first letter of our booking code?
examples.zh: 预约代码的第一个字母能确认一下吗，是「apple 开头的那个 A」？

collocations: say A as in apple
confirm A as in apple
clarify with A as in apple

words.zhGloss: 连续出现的两个相同字母
words.enDefinition: A pair of identical letters next to each other in a written word or name.
acceptedZhAnswers: 连续出现的两个相同字母

examples.en: The name has a double letter in the middle, so please check before you print it.
examples.zh: 这个名字中间「连续出现两个相同字母」，打印前请确认一下。

examples.en: I forgot the double letter when I entered the street name into the map again.
examples.zh: 我再次把街道名输入地图时，忘了那里有「连续出现的两个相同字母」。

collocations: write a double letter
check for a double letter
spell a name with a double letter

words.expression: could you type it in the chat
words.lemma: could you type it in the chat
words.zhGloss: 你能把它打在聊天框里吗
words.enDefinition: A request to enter spoken information as text in the chat area of a call or meeting.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你能把它打在聊天框里吗
acceptedEnVariants: could you type it in the chat

examples.en: Could you type it in the chat now so I can copy the address?
examples.zh: 「你能现在把它打在聊天框里吗」？我想复制一下地址。

examples.en: Could you type it in the chat because the room name is hard to hear?
examples.zh: 房间名称听不清，「你能把它打在聊天框里吗」？

collocations: could you type it in the chat for me
could you type it in the chat instead
could you type it in the chat now

words.expression: can you show me the word
words.lemma: can you show me the word
words.zhGloss: 你能给我看看那个词吗
words.enDefinition: A request to see a word written down so you can identify or understand it.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你能给我看看那个词吗
acceptedEnVariants: can you show me the word

examples.en: Can you show me the word on your screen so I know which spelling you mean?
examples.zh: 「你能给我看看屏幕上的那个词吗」？我想知道你说的是哪种拼法。

examples.en: Can you show me the word in the guide before we start looking for the sign?
examples.zh: 开始找牌子前，「你能给我看看指南里的那个词吗」？

collocations: can you show me the word in the guide
can you show me the word on your screen
can you show me the word on the label

words.expression: that's not how I heard it
words.lemma: that's not how i heard it
words.enDefinition: Used when your understanding of what was said differs from someone else's account.
acceptedEnVariants: that's not how I heard it

examples.en: That's not how I heard it when the driver explained the stop outside the library.
examples.zh: 司机在图书馆外说明站点时，「我听到的不是那样」。

examples.en: That's not how I heard it, so let's ask her which entrance she meant.
examples.zh: 「我听到的不是那样」，我们问问她指的是哪个入口吧。

collocations: say that's not how I heard it
that's not how I heard it at the time
that's not how I heard it from reception

words.enDefinition: A way of pronouncing words that you have not often heard before.

examples.en: I needed a moment to get used to an unfamiliar accent on the recorded guide.
examples.zh: 我花了点时间才适应录音导览里「不熟悉的口音」。

examples.en: I asked her to repeat the street name because it was spoken in an unfamiliar accent.
examples.zh: 对方念街道名用了我「不熟悉的口音」，我请她再说了一遍。

collocations: hear an unfamiliar accent
get used to an unfamiliar accent
listen to an unfamiliar accent

words.enDefinition: A way of pronouncing a word or sound commonly associated with a particular region.

examples.en: The driver used a regional pronunciation of the station name that I hadn't heard before.
examples.zh: 司机用的车站名「地方读法」是我以前没听过的。

examples.en: My neighbour explained the regional pronunciation after I recognised the name on the street sign.
examples.zh: 我看到路牌认出了那个名字，邻居就给我解释了这个「地方读法」。

collocations: hear a regional pronunciation
explain a regional pronunciation
get used to a regional pronunciation

words.enDefinition: To say the first syllable of a word with greater emphasis than the other syllables.

examples.en: The guide asked us to stress the first syllable when we said the village name.
examples.zh: 导游请我们说村名时「重读第一个音节」。

examples.en: I forgot to stress the first syllable, so my friend thought I meant another word.
examples.zh: 我忘了「重读第一个音节」，朋友以为我说的是另一个词。

collocations: remember to stress the first syllable
usually stress the first syllable
stress the first syllable when you say it

words.enDefinition: Used to say you have noticed a similar sound in two or more words.

examples.en: These words sound alike to me when someone says them quickly over the phone.
examples.zh: 有人在电话里说得很快时，我觉得「这两个词听起来很像」。

examples.en: These words sound alike on the recording, but they refer to two different stations.
examples.zh: 录音里「这两个词听起来很像」，但指的是两个不同的车站。

collocations: these words sound alike to me
these words sound alike on the recording
explain why these words sound alike

words.expression: did you say fifteen or fifty
words.lemma: did you say fifteen or fifty
words.zhGloss: 你说的是十五还是五十
words.enDefinition: A sample question for checking which of two similar-sounding numbers you heard.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你说的是十五还是五十
acceptedEnVariants: did you say fifteen or fifty

examples.en: Did you say fifteen or fifty minutes for the walk from the station to campus?
examples.zh: 从车站走到校园，「你说的是十五还是五十分钟」？

examples.en: Did you say fifteen or fifty people when you called about our room booking today?
examples.zh: 今天你打电话说我们订房间的事时，「说的是十五还是五十人」？

collocations: did you say fifteen or fifty minutes
did you say fifteen or fifty people
did you say fifteen or fifty seats

words.enDefinition: Used when you stop hearing any voice or sound on the phone line.

examples.en: The line went quiet just after you said my name, so I thought we'd been disconnected.
examples.zh: 你刚说完我的名字，「电话里突然没声了」，我以为断线了。

examples.en: The line went quiet while I was giving you the building number for tonight's meeting.
examples.zh: 我正告诉你今晚开会的楼号，「电话里突然没声了」。

collocations: the line went quiet for a moment
the line went quiet after the transfer
say the line went quiet

words.expression: there's a bit of an echo
words.lemma: there's a bit of an echo
words.enDefinition: Used to tell someone that part of the sound you hear repeats with a delay.
acceptedEnVariants: there's a bit of an echo

examples.en: There's a bit of an echo on this call when both laptops are on speaker.
examples.zh: 两台笔记本电脑都开免提时，通话里「有一点回声」。

examples.en: There's a bit of an echo in here, so I might ask you to repeat things.
examples.zh: 这里「有一点回声」，所以我可能会请你把话再说一遍。

collocations: there's a bit of an echo in here
there's a bit of an echo on my end
there's a bit of an echo on this call

words.zhGloss: 你刚才重读的是哪个词
words.enDefinition: A question asking which word in a phrase someone emphasised to convey their meaning.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你刚才重读的是哪个词

examples.en: Which word did you stress when you told us to leave the small room unlocked?
examples.zh: 你让我们别锁小房间时，「刚才重读的是哪个词」？

examples.en: Which word did you stress in that sentence about who should bring the blue box?
examples.zh: 你说该由谁带蓝箱子那句话里，「重读的是哪个词」？

collocations: which word did you stress in that sentence
ask which word did you stress
which word did you stress when you repeated it

words.expression: is that a zero or the letter O
words.lemma: is that a zero or the letter o
words.enDefinition: A question for telling the similar-looking digit 0 and letter O apart in a written string.
acceptedEnVariants: is that a zero or the letter O

examples.en: Is that a zero or the letter O at the end of the reference number?
examples.zh: 查询编号最后一位「是零还是字母 O」？

examples.en: Is that a zero or the letter O beside the first dash in the code?
examples.zh: 代码里第一道短横线旁边「是零还是字母 O」？

collocations: is that a zero or the letter O in your code
ask is that a zero or the letter O
is that a zero or the letter O at the end

words.expression: can I jump in for a second
words.lemma: can i jump in for a second
words.enDefinition: A casual request to take a short turn in a conversation already in progress.
acceptedEnVariants: can I jump in for a second

examples.en: Can I jump in for a second before we decide where to meet tomorrow?
examples.zh: 决定明天见面地点前，「我能插一句吗」？

examples.en: Can I jump in for a second because I think we've got two different room numbers?
examples.zh: 我觉得我们记的是两个不同的房间号，「我能插一句吗」？

collocations: can I jump in for a second about that date
can I jump in for a second here
can I jump in for a second before we move on

words.enDefinition: A polite way to pause another person's explanation at a particular point, often to clarify it.

examples.en: Could I stop you there to check which gate the coach is leaving from?
examples.zh: 「我能先打断你一下吗」？我想确认长途车从哪个门口出发。

examples.en: Could I stop you there for a moment while I write down the new date?
examples.zh: 「我能先打断你一下吗」？让我先记下新日期。

collocations: could I stop you there for a moment
could I stop you there to check something
could I stop you there before we go on

words.enDefinition: Used to mark that you want to say or check something before the speaker continues.

examples.en: Before you go on, can you tell me how far that stop is from campus?
examples.zh: 「在你接着说之前」，你能先告诉我那个站离校园多远吗？

examples.en: Before you go on to the next step, I'll make sure my tablet is ready.
examples.zh: 「在你接着讲下一步之前」，我先确认我的平板准备好了。

collocations: before you go on, can I check
before you go on, let me ask
before you go on to the next step

words.expression: one thing before we move on
words.lemma: one thing before we move on
words.zhGloss: 接着说之前还有一件事
words.enDefinition: A short way to introduce a remaining point before people switch topics or start something new.
acceptedZhAnswers: 接着说之前还有一件事
acceptedEnVariants: one thing before we move on

examples.en: One thing before we move on to the next room, where should I return this key?
examples.zh: 「去下一个房间前还有一件事」，我该去哪里还这把钥匙？

examples.en: One thing before we move on, are there any extra places for Friday's trip yet?
examples.zh: 「接着说之前还有一件事」，周五的出行现在还有空位吗？

collocations: one thing before we move on to the next topic
one thing before we move on to the next item
mention one thing before we move on

words.enDefinition: An opening that signals you want to ask something briefly without taking much time.

examples.en: Just a quick question before you leave, what time does the last bus go?
examples.zh: 你走之前，「我就问一句」，最后一班车几点发车？

examples.en: Just a quick question about this step, should I leave the space under my name blank?
examples.zh: 关于这一步「我就问一句」，名字下面那格需要留空吗？

collocations: just a quick question about the date
just a quick question before you leave
just a quick question about this step

words.enDefinition: A polite opening before interrupting someone when you would normally prefer to wait.

examples.en: I hate to interrupt, but we need to know whether the back gate is open.
examples.zh: 「不好意思打断一下」，我们得知道后门开没开。

examples.en: I hate to interrupt, but I think she's waiting to ask us something important.
examples.zh: 「不好意思打断一下」，我觉得她正等着问重要的事。

collocations: I hate to interrupt, but
I hate to interrupt right now
I hate to interrupt your conversation

words.zhGloss: 这个话题待会儿接着说
words.enDefinition: A request to pause and remember what you want to say so you can come back to it.
acceptedZhAnswers: 这个话题待会儿接着说

examples.en: Could you hold that thought while I check who's calling from the front desk?
examples.zh: 我先看看前台是谁打来的电话，你能「待会儿接着说这件事」吗？

examples.en: Hold that thought until we get inside, where I can hear your idea properly.
examples.zh: 「进去再接着说这件事吧」，里面我就能听清你的想法了。

collocations: hold that thought for a moment
hold that thought until I get back
can you hold that thought

words.enDefinition: A request to continue until you have finished what you are saying.

examples.en: Please let me finish before we decide who should meet the visitors downstairs tonight.
examples.zh: 决定今晚谁去楼下接访客之前，「请让我说完」。

examples.en: Let me finish this point, and then we can talk about what you would change.
examples.zh: 「让我先讲完这一点」，然后我们再谈你想改什么。

collocations: let me finish my sentence
let me finish this point
please let me finish

words.enDefinition: A way to tell someone that you had more to say when they took over the conversation.

examples.en: I wasn't finished when the others moved on to deciding what to bring on Saturday.
examples.zh: 其他人转去商量周六带什么时，「我刚才还没说完」。

examples.en: I wasn't finished with the directions when the driver turned left at the lights.
examples.zh: 司机在红绿灯处左转时，「我还没把路线说完」。

collocations: I wasn't finished with that point
I wasn't finished speaking
tell them I wasn't finished

words.expression: can I take it from here
words.lemma: can i take it from here
words.enDefinition: A request to take over an explanation or task at its current point.
acceptedEnVariants: can I take it from here

examples.en: Can I take it from here now that you've reached the part about the map?
examples.zh: 你已经讲到地图那部分了，「接下来能换我来说吗」？

examples.en: Can I take it from here and explain how the second group should come in?
examples.zh: 「接下来能换我来说吗」？我来解释第二组该怎么进来。

collocations: can I take it from here with the map
can I take it from here for a moment
ask can I take it from here

words.expression: I lost my train of thought
words.lemma: i lost my train of thought
words.zhGloss: 我一下子忘了刚才在说什么
words.enDefinition: Used when an interruption or pause makes you forget the idea you were about to continue.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我一下子忘了刚才在说什么
acceptedEnVariants: I lost my train of thought

examples.en: I lost my train of thought when the announcement came on just as I started speaking.
examples.zh: 我刚开口广播就响了，「我一下子忘了刚才在说什么」。

examples.en: I lost my train of thought, so remind me what we were discussing before the call.
examples.zh: 「我一下子忘了刚才在说什么」，提醒我通话前在讨论什么吧。

collocations: I lost my train of thought for a moment
I lost my train of thought halfway through
I lost my train of thought after the interruption

words.enDefinition: A question a speaker asks when trying to remember where they paused or were interrupted.

examples.en: Where was I before the delivery driver called about the boxes we were expecting?
examples.zh: 送货司机打电话问我们等的箱子之前，「我刚刚说到哪儿了」？

examples.en: Where was I again before we stopped to let those people walk past us?
examples.zh: 我们停下来让那些人先过去之前，「我刚刚说到哪儿了」？

collocations: where was I before the break
where was I again
ask where was I

words.enDefinition: Used to explain that you were exploring an idea in speech without making a decision or proposal.

examples.en: I was thinking aloud about the seating, so there's no need to move anything yet.
examples.zh: 座位的事「我只是边想边说」，先不用挪东西。

examples.en: I was thinking aloud when I mentioned closing the side entrance after six tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我提到明天六点后关侧门时，「只是边想边说」。

collocations: I was thinking aloud about the layout
say I was thinking aloud
I was thinking aloud at the time

words.zhGloss: 我们俩刚才同时开口了
words.enDefinition: Used to acknowledge that two speakers started talking at the same time.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们俩刚才同时开口了

examples.en: I think we both spoke at once when the receptionist paused to check our booking.
examples.zh: 接待员停下来核查预约时，我想「我们俩刚才同时开口了」。

examples.en: We both spoke at once, so I didn't hear what you asked about tomorrow.
examples.zh: 「我们俩刚才同时开口了」，所以我没听到你问明天的什么事。

collocations: we both spoke at once just then
I think we both spoke at once
laugh because we both spoke at once

words.enDefinition: Used to say you will wait until the other person completes what they are saying.

examples.en: I'll ask my question after you finish telling us what happened at the entrance.
examples.zh: 「等你讲完入口发生的事以后」，我再问问题。

examples.en: I can mention the bus times after you finish explaining where to meet everyone.
examples.zh: 「等你讲完大家该在哪里集合以后」，我再讲公交车时间。

collocations: ask after you finish
speak after you finish
check one thing after you finish

words.expression: I'll come to that in a minute
words.lemma: i'll come to that in a minute
words.enDefinition: Used to tell someone that you will deal with the point they raised shortly.
acceptedEnVariants: I'll come to that in a minute

examples.en: I'll come to that in a minute when I explain why the main entrance is closed.
examples.zh: 「我马上会讲到那一点」，会解释正门为什么关闭。

examples.en: I'll come to that in a minute after everyone has written down the contact number.
examples.zh: 等大家记下联系电话后，「我马上会讲到那一点」。

collocations: I'll come to that in a minute when we get to the dates
say I'll come to that in a minute
promise I'll come to that in a minute

words.zhGloss: 我们待会儿再回来说这点
words.enDefinition: A suggestion to return to a particular topic later in the same conversation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们待会儿再回来说这点

examples.en: Let's come back to that after Rosa arrives, because she knows where the keys are kept.
examples.zh: 罗莎到了以后，「我们再回来说这点」吧，她知道钥匙放在哪儿。

examples.en: Let's come back to that in a moment when we've agreed how to get there.
examples.zh: 等确定怎么去那里以后，「我们待会儿再回来说这点」。

collocations: let's come back to that after the break
let's come back to that in a moment
let's come back to that when everyone is here

words.expression: let me go back a step
words.lemma: let me go back a step
words.enDefinition: Used when a speaker wants to return to an earlier stage of an explanation.
acceptedEnVariants: let me go back a step

examples.en: Let me go back a step and explain why we need two separate lists tonight.
examples.zh: 「让我退回去说上一步」，解释为什么今晚需要两个名单。

examples.en: Let me go back a step before I show you where the map changes colour.
examples.zh: 给你看地图颜色在哪里变化之前，「让我退回去说上一步」。

collocations: let me go back a step to the beginning
let me go back a step before I explain
say let me go back a step

words.expression: I don't want to put words in your mouth
words.lemma: i don't want to put words in your mouth
words.zhGloss: 我不想擅自替你表达观点
words.enDefinition: Used before checking an interpretation because you want the other person to state their own view.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我不想擅自替你表达观点
acceptedEnVariants: I don't want to put words in your mouth

examples.en: I don't want to put words in your mouth, so please tell me what you meant.
examples.zh: 「我不想擅自替你表达观点」，所以请你告诉我刚才是什么意思。

examples.en: I don't want to put words in your mouth when I summarise our conversation for the group.
examples.zh: 我给小组概括这次谈话时，「不想擅自替你表达观点」。

collocations: I don't want to put words in your mouth about this
I don't want to put words in your mouth here
I don't want to put words in your mouth when I summarise

words.enDefinition: A way to invite someone to continue speaking, often by reminding them about their previous point.

examples.en: You were saying something about the side entrance before the coach drove past us.
examples.zh: 长途车从我们旁边开过去之前，「你刚才说到」侧门的事。

examples.en: You were saying we should meet by the smaller sign before the call dropped.
examples.zh: 电话断线前，「你刚才说到」我们该在小一点的牌子旁碰面。

collocations: you were saying something about the schedule
you were saying before the interruption
you were saying we should

words.expression: did you want to say something
words.lemma: did you want to say something
words.zhGloss: 你刚才是想说点什么吗
words.enDefinition: A question inviting someone to speak after it looks as though they tried to start.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你刚才是想说点什么吗
acceptedEnVariants: did you want to say something

examples.en: Did you want to say something before I tell the group where we're meeting?
examples.zh: 我告诉小组见面地点之前，「你刚才是想说点什么吗」？

examples.en: Did you want to say something about the schedule when we both started talking?
examples.zh: 刚才我们同时开口时，「你是想说点什么吗」？是关于日程的吗？

collocations: did you want to say something about the plan
did you want to say something before we go
ask did you want to say something

words.expression: there's more to it than that
words.lemma: there's more to it than that
words.enDefinition: Used to signal that the current explanation leaves out relevant details or complications.
acceptedEnVariants: there's more to it than that

examples.en: There's more to it than that because the last bus uses a different stop.
examples.zh: 「这件事还有别的情况」，因为末班公交用的是另一个站点。

examples.en: There's more to it than that, so let me show you both versions of the map.
examples.zh: 「这件事还有别的情况」，我给你看看两个版本的地图吧。

collocations: I'm sure there's more to it than that
say there's more to it than that
explain why there's more to it than that

words.enDefinition: Used to say that people should speak one after another so they can be heard.

examples.en: We need to speak one person at a time or the driver won't hear anyone.
examples.zh: 我们得「一次一个人说」，不然司机谁的话都听不清。

examples.en: One person at a time, please, so I can write down each person's address correctly.
examples.zh: 请「一次一个人说」，这样我能把每个人的地址记对。

collocations: let's speak one person at a time
ask for one person at a time
one person at a time, please

words.expression: I want to hear the rest
words.lemma: i want to hear the rest
words.enDefinition: Used to encourage someone to finish their story or explanation after a pause or interruption.
acceptedEnVariants: I want to hear the rest

examples.en: I want to hear the rest of the story after you finish answering the door.
examples.zh: 你去开完门回来，「后面的故事我还想听」。

examples.en: I want to hear the rest before we decide which version to put in the newsletter.
examples.zh: 决定把哪个版本放进通讯之前，「后面的内容我还想听」。

collocations: I want to hear the rest of the story
I want to hear the rest first
say I want to hear the rest

words.enDefinition: A short period when nobody is speaking during an exchange.

examples.en: I waited for a pause in the conversation before asking about the return time.
examples.zh: 我等到「对话出现停顿」，才问什么时间回来。

examples.en: There was a pause in the conversation while our friend opened the map again.
examples.zh: 朋友重新打开地图时，「对话出现了停顿」。

collocations: wait for a pause in the conversation
listen for a pause in the conversation
take advantage of a pause in the conversation

words.enDefinition: To pause between comments so that other people have an opportunity to speak.

examples.en: It's helpful to leave a gap after asking a question on a crowded call.
examples.zh: 通话人多时，提问后「留出开口的空当」有助于别人回应。

examples.en: Please leave a gap between stories so anyone who wants to can join the conversation.
examples.zh: 每讲完一个故事，请「留出开口的空当」，让想参与的人也能说话。

collocations: leave a gap for someone to speak
leave a gap after a question
leave a gap before moving on

words.enDefinition: To stop following the sequence or meaning of a conversation or explanation.

examples.en: I began to lose the thread when the directions switched from street names to landmarks.
examples.zh: 路线说明从街名转到地标时，我有点「跟不上对方的思路」了。

examples.en: It's easy to lose the thread if three people tell the same story at once.
examples.zh: 三个人同时讲同一件事，很容易「跟不上谈话的思路」。

collocations: lose the thread of a story
lose the thread halfway through
lose the thread of an explanation

words.enDefinition: To understand what people are talking about as the exchange continues.

examples.en: I could follow the conversation better once the group switched to a quieter table.
examples.zh: 小组换到更安静的桌子后，我更容易「跟上对话」。

examples.en: It was difficult to follow the conversation because I missed the name of the place.
examples.zh: 我没听到地点名，所以很难「跟上对话」。

collocations: struggle to follow the conversation
easier to follow the conversation
help someone follow the conversation

words.enDefinition: Used to say that a group stopped speaking, often at the same moment.

examples.en: Everyone went quiet after the question, so I waited to see if anyone would answer.
examples.zh: 问题一提出来，「大家都安静下来了」，我就等着看有没有人回答。

examples.en: Everyone went quiet for a moment before Alex explained what the sign actually meant.
examples.zh: 「大家都安静了一会儿」，然后亚历克斯解释了牌子到底是什么意思。

collocations: everyone went quiet after the question
everyone went quiet for a moment
notice that everyone went quiet

words.enDefinition: A request for the person you are listening to to continue what they were saying.

examples.en: Please go on with your story now that everybody has finished finding a seat.
examples.zh: 大家现在都坐好了，「请接着说」你的故事。

examples.en: Please go on where you left off before we had to move the chairs.
examples.zh: 刚才我们要挪椅子，你就停了下来，「请接着说」吧。

collocations: please go on with your story
please go on where you left off
say please go on

words.expression: I didn't mean to cut you off
words.lemma: i didn't mean to cut you off
words.enDefinition: Used to acknowledge an unintentional interruption and leave the other person room to continue speaking.
acceptedEnVariants: I didn't mean to cut you off

examples.en: I didn't mean to cut you off while you were explaining the meeting point.
examples.zh: 你正在解释集合地点，「我不是故意打断你的」。

examples.en: I didn't mean to cut you off earlier when you were telling us about the route.
examples.zh: 刚才你正在跟我们说路线，「我不是故意打断你的」。

collocations: I didn't mean to cut you off there
I didn't mean to cut you off earlier
I didn't mean to cut you off mid-sentence

words.expression: jump in if I'm missing something
words.lemma: jump in if i'm missing something
words.zhGloss: 我有遗漏的话就请补充
words.enDefinition: An invitation for people to interrupt briefly if important information is being left out.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我有遗漏的话就请补充
acceptedEnVariants: jump in if I'm missing something

examples.en: Jump in if I'm missing something important as I explain the directions to everyone.
examples.zh: 我在给大家说明路线时，「我有遗漏的话就请补充」。

examples.en: Jump in if I'm missing something about the timings when I repeat the plan.
examples.zh: 我复述计划时，「如果我漏了什么时间点，就请补充」。

collocations: jump in if I'm missing something important
jump in if I'm missing something about the timings
tell the others to jump in if I'm missing something

words.enDefinition: To give someone the opportunity to continue speaking after taking a turn yourself.

examples.en: I'll pass it back to you once I've explained why the first time won't work.
examples.zh: 解释完为什么第一个时间不合适，我就「再请你接着说」。

examples.en: Let me state the new date before I pass it back to you to finish.
examples.zh: 让我先说一下新日期，然后「再请你接着说」，把话说完。

collocations: I'll pass it back to you
pass it back to you after one point
pass it back to you to finish

words.zhGloss: 我刚才引用的是别人的话
words.enDefinition: Used to clarify that words you repeated came from another person and were not your own statement.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我刚才引用的是别人的话

examples.en: I was quoting someone else when I called the smaller room unsuitable for the event.
examples.zh: 我说小房间不适合办活动时，「刚才引用的是别人的话」。

examples.en: I was quoting someone else from the meeting, so let me explain what I actually think.
examples.zh: 「我刚才引用的是会上别人的话」，让我说说自己实际是怎么想的。

collocations: I was quoting someone else in that message
say I was quoting someone else
explain that I was quoting someone else

words.enDefinition: A question asking which thing, person, or earlier statement someone has in mind.

examples.en: What are you referring to when you say we need the old one back?
examples.zh: 你说我们得把旧的拿回来，「你指的是什么」？

examples.en: What are you referring to on this list when you mention the spare equipment?
examples.zh: 你提到备用设备时，「指的是这份清单上的哪一项」？

collocations: what are you referring to on this list
what are you referring to exactly
ask what are you referring to

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify a particular thing among several possibilities.

examples.en: Which one do you mean, the big box by the door or the smaller one?
examples.zh: 「你指的是哪一个」，门边的大箱子还是小一点的那个？

examples.en: Which one do you mean on the map when you say the main staircase?
examples.zh: 你说主楼梯时，「指的是地图上的哪一个」？

collocations: which one do you mean on the shelf
which one do you mean on the map
ask which one do you mean

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify the person currently being discussed.

examples.en: Who are we talking about when you mention the person who opened the hall first?
examples.zh: 你说最早开大厅的那个人，「我们说的是谁」？

examples.en: Who are we talking about here, your flatmate or the person from the upstairs flat?
examples.zh: 「我们说的是谁」，你的室友还是住楼上的那个人？

collocations: who are we talking about here
who are we talking about in this story
ask who are we talking about

words.enDefinition: A question checking whether something just mentioned is the one already discussed.

examples.en: Is that the same one that had a yellow sticker on the lid yesterday?
examples.zh: 「那是同一个吗」，就是昨天盖子上贴着黄色贴纸的那个？

examples.en: Is that the same one you set aside for me after the meeting last week?
examples.zh: 「那是同一个吗」，就是上周开完会你给我留的那个？

collocations: is that the same one you showed me earlier
is that the same one on the list
is that the same one as before

words.enDefinition: A question checking if the group or rule just mentioned applies to you personally.

examples.en: Does that include me if I'm only helping to carry a few things upstairs?
examples.zh: 如果我只是帮忙把几件东西搬到楼上，「这也包括我吗」？

examples.en: Does that include me too now that I've changed my plans for Friday evening?
examples.zh: 既然我改了周五晚上的安排，「这也包括我吗」？

collocations: does that include me as a volunteer
does that include me this time
does that include me too

words.enDefinition: With the opposite order, direction, or relationship from the one stated.

examples.en: I meant the other way round when I said which shelf the pans go on.
examples.zh: 说到锅放哪一层时，「我说的是反过来」。

examples.en: It was the other way round because Maya lent me the chair last week.
examples.zh: 实际是「反过来」，上周是玛雅把椅子借给我。

collocations: mean the other way round
do it the other way round
have it the other way round

words.expression: do you mean now or later
words.lemma: do you mean now or later
words.zhGloss: 你的意思是现在还是稍后
words.enDefinition: A direct question checking whether someone means immediately or at a later time.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你的意思是现在还是稍后
acceptedEnVariants: do you mean now or later

examples.en: Do you mean now or later this evening when there are fewer people around?
examples.zh: 「你的意思是现在还是稍后」，晚一点人少了再说？

examples.en: Do you mean now or later when you ask me to bring the boxes downstairs?
examples.zh: 你让我把箱子搬下楼，「你的意思是现在还是稍后」？

collocations: do you mean now or later this evening
do you mean now or later today
ask do you mean now or later

words.expression: which part are you talking about
words.lemma: which part are you talking about
words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to point out the section or stage they mean.
acceptedEnVariants: which part are you talking about

examples.en: Which part are you talking about when you say the video was hard to follow?
examples.zh: 你说视频很难看懂，「说的是哪一部分」？

examples.en: Which part are you talking about, the first paragraph or the note at the bottom?
examples.zh: 「你说的是哪一部分」，第一段还是底部的注释？

collocations: which part are you talking about in the instructions
which part are you talking about exactly
ask which part are you talking about

words.enDefinition: A question used to ask someone to explain the particular meaning of an expression in context.

examples.en: In what sense is the new room better if it fits fewer people than before?
examples.zh: 新房间能容纳的人少些，「在哪方面」说它更好呢？

examples.en: Could you explain in what sense this door is the main entrance for visitors?
examples.zh: 你能解释一下「在哪种意义上」这扇门算访客的正门吗？

collocations: in what sense is it different
in what sense do you mean it
ask in what sense

words.enDefinition: A question asking what full name or phrase a letter or abbreviation represents.

examples.en: What does that stand for in the message you sent about tomorrow's rehearsal time?
examples.zh: 你发的明天排练时间的消息里，「这是哪几个词的缩写」？

examples.en: What does that stand for on the board where the old room number was written?
examples.zh: 以前板上写旧房间号的地方，「现在的字母是哪几个词的缩写」？

collocations: what does that stand for on the form
what does that stand for in this list
ask what does that stand for

words.enDefinition: Used to indicate that a shorter name or set of letters represents a longer form.

examples.en: I asked whether the name on the door was short for something more familiar.
examples.zh: 我问门上那名字是不是某个更常见名称的「简写」。

examples.en: The name on the schedule is short for the group that looks after the garden.
examples.zh: 日程表上的名字是负责照看花园的那个小组名称的「简写」。

collocations: be short for a name
be short for the full title
ask what it's short for

words.expression: what does that mean in practice
words.lemma: what does that mean in practice
words.enDefinition: A question asking how an idea, instruction, or rule works in a real situation.
acceptedEnVariants: what does that mean in practice

examples.en: What does that mean in practice for people who share the kitchen with another flat?
examples.zh: 和另一户合用厨房的人「实际会怎么做」？

examples.en: What does that mean in practice if we all need to collect our keys separately?
examples.zh: 如果我们得各自领钥匙，「具体到实际是怎样的」？

collocations: what does that mean in practice for us
what does that mean in practice here
ask what does that mean in practice

words.enDefinition: A polite request for precise details instead of a broad or general statement.

examples.en: Could you be more specific about which cupboard you want us to leave empty?
examples.zh: 「你能说得具体一点吗」？哪个柜子需要我们腾空？

examples.en: Could you be more specific about which set of cables goes with this projector?
examples.zh: 「你能说得具体一点吗」？哪一套线跟这台投影仪配套？

collocations: could you be more specific about the time
could you be more specific about what changed
could you be more specific for us

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify the particular changes they just referred to.

examples.en: What exactly changed in the instructions for returning dishes to the shared kitchen this week?
examples.zh: 这周把盘子放回共用厨房的说明「具体有什么变动」？

examples.en: What exactly changed between the message I saw and the one sent out this morning?
examples.zh: 我看到的消息和今天上午发的那条，内容「具体有什么变动」？

collocations: what exactly changed on the form
what exactly changed since yesterday
ask what exactly changed

words.expression: how specific do I need to be
words.lemma: how specific do i need to be
words.enDefinition: A question asking how much detail the listener expects you to give.
acceptedEnVariants: how specific do I need to be

examples.en: How specific do I need to be when I explain where the keys were found?
examples.zh: 我说明钥匙在哪儿找到时，「需要说得多具体」？

examples.en: How specific do I need to be about the dates when I tell the club?
examples.zh: 我告诉俱乐部时，关于日期「需要说得多具体」？

collocations: how specific do I need to be about dates
how specific do I need to be about my plans
ask how specific do I need to be

words.expression: could you give me an example
words.lemma: could you give me an example
words.enDefinition: A polite request for a particular case that makes an idea easier to understand.
acceptedEnVariants: could you give me an example

examples.en: Could you give me an example of what counts as a large item for collection?
examples.zh: 「你能给我举个例子吗」？回收时什么样的东西算大件？

examples.en: Could you give me an example of the kind of message you want us to send?
examples.zh: 「你能给我举个例子吗」？就说你想让我们发哪种消息。

collocations: could you give me an example of that
could you give me an example from yesterday
could you give me an example before we start

words.enDefinition: A short follow-up question asking for examples of something just mentioned in general terms.

examples.en: Such as what, apart from chairs and tables that we already have upstairs?
examples.zh: 楼上已经有椅子和桌子了，除此之外「比如什么」？

examples.en: She asked, “Such as what?” when I mentioned extra things we might need to bring.
examples.zh: 我提到我们可能得多带些东西，她问「比如什么」？

collocations: ask such as what
say such as what
ask someone such as what

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone for the general type of thing, activity, or situation they mean.

examples.en: What sort of thing do you have in mind for the space near the door?
examples.zh: 对于门边那块地方，「你想放什么样的东西」？

examples.en: I asked what sort of thing would count as an extra task for the volunteers.
examples.zh: 我问，「什么样的事情」算志愿者的额外任务。

collocations: what sort of thing do you have in mind
ask what sort of thing
what sort of thing would count

words.expression: could you show me how that works
words.lemma: could you show me how that works
words.zhGloss: 你能演示一下怎么用吗
words.enDefinition: A request to see how a tool, system, or process works in action.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你能演示一下怎么用吗
acceptedEnVariants: could you show me how that works

examples.en: Could you show me how that works before I try to fold the stand myself?
examples.zh: 我自己尝试把架子折起来前，「你能演示一下怎么用吗」？

examples.en: Could you show me how that works on your phone before I open the app?
examples.zh: 我打开应用之前，「你能在你手机上演示一下怎么用吗」？

collocations: could you show me how that works in person
could you show me how that works on your phone
could you show me how that works first

words.enDefinition: To explain a process or situation to someone while moving through its stages with them.

examples.en: Could you talk me through it while I set up the projector for tonight?
examples.zh: 我准备今晚的投影仪时，你能「带我一步一步弄明白」吗？

examples.en: My neighbour offered to talk me through it before I organised my first clothing swap.
examples.zh: 在我第一次组织衣物交换活动前，邻居提出「带我一步一步弄明白」。

collocations: talk me through it from the start
could you talk me through it
offer to talk me through it

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to describe the details of a proposed idea or situation.

examples.en: What would that look like on the day if we meet people at two entrances?
examples.zh: 如果我们在两个入口接人，「当天具体会是什么样」？

examples.en: What would that look like for someone who has never been to our building?
examples.zh: 对从没来过这栋楼的人来说，「具体会是什么样」？

collocations: what would that look like on the day
what would that look like for us
ask what would that look like

words.enDefinition: Used to identify a particular part of an explanation by mentioning what it was about.

examples.en: I missed the part about where to collect the spare keys for the common room.
examples.zh: 我没听清「关于去哪儿领取公共休息室备用钥匙的那部分」。

examples.en: Could we go over the part about which guests need to sign the visitor list?
examples.zh: 「关于哪些访客要在来访登记表上签名的那部分」，我们能再过一遍吗？

collocations: miss the part about the costs
repeat the part about the address
go over the part about timing

words.enDefinition: A question asking for the next step, line, or event immediately following the one just mentioned.

examples.en: What comes right after that step where you check the number on the back?
examples.zh: 查背面数字那一步，「之后紧接着是什么」？

examples.en: Could you show me what comes right after that in the instructions on the box?
examples.zh: 你能给我看看包装盒的说明里，「那之后紧接着是什么」吗？

collocations: what comes right after that step
ask what comes right after that
show me what comes right after that

words.expression: do I need the exact wording
words.lemma: do i need the exact wording
words.enDefinition: A question checking whether the precise words matter or whether a summary is enough.
acceptedEnVariants: do I need the exact wording

examples.en: Do I need the exact wording from the sign or just the new opening hours?
examples.zh: 牌子上的内容，「我需要记下原话吗」，还是只要记新的开放时间？

examples.en: Do I need the exact wording here, or can I explain it in my own words?
examples.zh: 这里「我需要记下原话吗」，还是可以用自己的话解释？

collocations: do I need the exact wording from the message
do I need the exact wording here
ask do I need the exact wording

words.enDefinition: An opening used to repeat a word or phrase you want the speaker to explain.

examples.en: When you say upstairs, do you mean the first landing or the floor above it?
examples.zh: 「你说楼上的时候」，指的是第一处楼梯平台，还是再上一层？

examples.en: When you say the next meeting, are you talking about Friday or next week?
examples.zh: 「你说下次碰面的时候」，指的是周五还是下周？

collocations: when you say upstairs
when you say it's close
when you say the next meeting

words.enDefinition: Used when asking what qualifies as a particular kind of thing under a description or rule.

examples.en: We asked what counts as a guest when people from other flats come over for dinner.
examples.zh: 其他公寓的人来吃饭时，我们问「什么样的人算客人」。

examples.en: Could you explain what counts as enough notice for changing the rehearsal time with everyone?
examples.zh: 需要跟大家改排练时间时，你能解释一下「提前多久通知算够」吗？

collocations: what counts as a guest
what counts as a large item
ask what counts as enough notice

words.enDefinition: A request to reduce the possible meanings, times, places, or other choices to a smaller set.

examples.en: Can you narrow it down to a day so I know when to be home?
examples.zh: 「你能缩小到具体哪一天吗」？这样我就知道什么时候要在家。

examples.en: Can you narrow it down a little so we know which building to look in?
examples.zh: 「你能把范围缩小一点吗」？这样我们就知道到哪栋楼去找。

collocations: can you narrow it down to a day
can you narrow it down to two choices
can you narrow it down a little

words.enDefinition: A question asking what evidence or reasoning led someone to make a particular statement.

examples.en: What makes you say that the keys have to stay in this drawer overnight?
examples.zh: 「你为什么这么说」，觉得钥匙晚上得留在这个抽屉里？

examples.en: What makes you say that the new labels will confuse people using the washing machines?
examples.zh: 「你为什么觉得」新标签会让用洗衣机的人看不明白？

collocations: what makes you say that about the room
what makes you say that now
ask what makes you say that

words.enDefinition: A question asking what information or assumptions supported an estimate, judgement, or claim already mentioned.

examples.en: What was that based on, the number of people invited or the people who replied?
examples.zh: 「那是根据什么得出的」，是受邀人数还是已经回复的人数？

examples.en: The estimate seemed too high, so I asked, “What was that based on?” as we walked out.
examples.zh: 估算看起来偏高，所以我们边走出去，我边问「那是根据什么得出的」？

collocations: what was that based on at the time
what was that based on exactly
ask what was that based on

words.enDefinition: To provide background details so someone can understand a comment or situation.

examples.en: Could you give me some context before I read the message from the organiser?
examples.zh: 我读组织者的消息之前，你能「给我讲讲前因后果」吗？

examples.en: My friend tried to give me some context about the change before everyone else arrived.
examples.zh: 其他人到之前，朋友试着「给我讲讲变更的前因后果」。

collocations: could you give me some context
give me some context before I answer
give me some context for that comment

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to explain how two points, events, or ideas are related.

examples.en: What's the connection between the extra keys and the change to the guest list?
examples.zh: 多出来的钥匙和宾客名单的改动，「这之间有什么关系」？

examples.en: What's the connection here between how many people came and which door was open?
examples.zh: 来的人数和开的是哪扇门，「这之间有什么关系」？

collocations: what's the connection between the two
what's the connection here
ask what's the connection

words.enDefinition: A question checking whether a rule or explanation applies to the case now being discussed.

examples.en: Does that apply here too if we share the kitchen with a different floor?
examples.zh: 如果我们跟另一层的人合用厨房，「这也适用于这里吗」？

examples.en: Does that apply here when the people using the room have an evening booking?
examples.zh: 使用房间的人订的是晚间时段，「这也适用于这里吗」？

collocations: does that apply here as well
does that apply here in our building
ask does that apply here

words.expression: tell me where I lost you
words.lemma: tell me where i lost you
words.zhGloss: 告诉我你从哪里开始没跟上
words.enDefinition: A request for the listener to identify the place where your explanation stopped making sense to them.
acceptedZhAnswers: 告诉我你从哪里开始没跟上
acceptedEnVariants: tell me where I lost you

examples.en: Can you tell me where I lost you in my explanation of the new schedule?
examples.zh: 我刚解释了新日程，你能「告诉我你从哪一段开始没听明白」吗？

examples.en: Tell me where I lost you so I can repeat that part more slowly.
examples.zh: 「告诉我你从哪里开始没跟上」，我好慢一点重讲那一段。

collocations: tell me where I lost you in the explanation
could you tell me where I lost you
tell me where I lost you on the map

words.enDefinition: Used to check your interpretation as you react to an explanation that is still going on.

examples.en: If I'm following you, the two boxes go upstairs and the rest stay by the door.
examples.zh: 「如果我理解对了」，两个箱子搬到楼上，其余的都留在门边。

examples.en: If I'm following you so far, we won't know the exact time until tomorrow afternoon.
examples.zh: 「如果到目前为止我理解对了」，我们得等到明天下午才知道确切时间。

collocations: if I'm following you correctly
if I'm following you so far
if I'm following you right

words.expression: let me check I've got this right
words.lemma: let me check i've got this right
words.zhGloss: 让我确认一下有没有理解对
words.enDefinition: Used when you want to repeat details in your own words to check your understanding.
acceptedZhAnswers: 让我确认一下有没有理解对
acceptedEnVariants: let me check I've got this right
let me check I got this right

examples.en: Let me check I've got this right before I put the dates on our calendar.
examples.zh: 「让我确认一下有没有理解对」，然后再把日期记到日历上。

examples.en: Let me check I've got this right, two people on each side of the display?
examples.zh: 「让我确认一下有没有理解对」，展台两边各站两个人？

collocations: let me check I've got this right first
let me check I've got this right before we go
say let me check I've got this right

words.enDefinition: An opening for summarising what you think the other person was trying to say.

examples.en: So what you're saying is that we can borrow the stand but need our own cables.
examples.zh: 「所以你的意思是」，我们可以借架子，但电线得自己带。

examples.en: So what you're saying is that the name changed and the location stayed the same.
examples.zh: 「所以你的意思是」，名字变了，但位置没变。

collocations: so what you're saying is that we start here
so what you're saying is that it depends
check what you're saying is

words.expression: have I got the order right
words.lemma: have i got the order right
words.enDefinition: A question checking whether you have understood or repeated the sequence correctly.
acceptedEnVariants: have I got the order right

examples.en: Have I got the order right if I put the larger box on the table first?
examples.zh: 如果我先把较大的箱子放在桌上，「我把顺序弄对了吗」？

examples.en: Have I got the order right this time, or should we collect the badges first?
examples.zh: 「这次我把顺序弄对了吗」，还是应该先去领徽章？

collocations: have I got the order right this time
have I got the order right for tomorrow
ask have I got the order right

words.enDefinition: Used to clarify that what you said was intended as a question rather than a statement.

examples.en: That was a question about the time, so I haven't booked anything for Friday yet.
examples.zh: 时间的事「我刚才是在问」，周五还什么都没订。

examples.en: That was a question for both of you about whether we should lock the cupboard.
examples.zh: 「我刚才是在问你们两位」，柜子要不要锁上。

collocations: that was a question about the time
explain that was a question
that was a question for both of you

words.zhGloss: 我这样理解那句话对吗
words.enDefinition: A question checking whether your interpretation of written information is right.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我这样理解那句话对吗

examples.en: Am I reading that correctly on the sign about where to leave the spare chairs?
examples.zh: 牌子上说了备用椅子放哪儿，「我这样理解那句话对吗」？

examples.en: Am I reading that correctly, or does it mean the room only closes on weekends?
examples.zh: 「我这样理解那句话对吗」，还是它的意思是房间只在周末关闭？

collocations: am I reading that correctly on the sign
am I reading that correctly this time
ask am I reading that correctly

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to show the point where your interpretation or reasoning became incorrect.

examples.en: Where did I go wrong when I tried to repeat the directions from the map?
examples.zh: 我试着复述地图上的路线时，「哪里理解错了」？

examples.en: Where did I go wrong in my explanation of which drawer the keys belong in?
examples.zh: 我说明钥匙该放哪个抽屉时，「哪里理解错了」？

collocations: where did I go wrong in my explanation
where did I go wrong this time
ask where did I go wrong

words.enDefinition: To express the same idea using different words, often to make it easier to understand.

examples.en: Could you put that another way because I don't recognise the word you used?
examples.zh: 我不认识你用的那个词，你能「换种说法」吗？

examples.en: Let me put that another way so it makes sense to someone new here.
examples.zh: 「我换种说法」，这样刚到这里的人也能听懂。

collocations: could you put that another way
let me put that another way
try to put that another way

words.enDefinition: Using the way you naturally express an idea without repeating someone else's exact wording.

examples.en: I'll explain it in my own words so you can check what I understood.
examples.zh: 我会「用我自己的话」解释一下，你看看我理解得对不对。

examples.en: I tried to repeat the instructions in my own words while we walked home.
examples.zh: 走回家时，我试着「用我自己的话」复述那些指示。

collocations: explain it in my own words
say it in my own words
repeat the directions in my own words

words.enDefinition: An opening for giving a particular case that illustrates what you just said.

examples.en: One example would be the smaller gate, which is only open during the afternoon.
examples.zh: 「举个例子就是」那个小门，它只在下午开放。

examples.en: One example would be leaving the large pans on the lower shared shelf after cooking.
examples.zh: 「举个例子就是」做完饭后，把大锅放在下面的共用架子上。

collocations: one example would be the side gate
one example would be the kitchen list
say one example would be

words.enDefinition: Using ordinary words that a person without specialist knowledge can understand.

examples.en: Could you explain it in plain language before we share it with the rest of the group?
examples.zh: 发给小组其他人前，你能「用通俗的话」解释一下吗？

examples.en: I asked for the rule in plain language because the notice used several technical terms.
examples.zh: 通知用了几个专业术语，所以我请对方「用通俗的话」讲讲这条规定。

collocations: say it in plain language
explain something in plain language
rewrite it in plain language

words.zhGloss: 那句话说的是字面意思
words.enDefinition: Used to clarify that the exact meaning of a statement was intended, without exaggeration or figurative language.
acceptedZhAnswers: 那句话说的是字面意思

examples.en: That was meant literally when I said the snow had covered the whole front step.
examples.zh: 我说雪把整个门前台阶盖住了，「那句话说的是字面意思」。

examples.en: That was meant literally, so please leave a hand's width between the two boxes.
examples.zh: 「那句话说的是字面意思」，所以两个箱子之间请真留出一掌宽的空隙。

collocations: explain that was meant literally
say that was meant literally
ask whether that was meant literally

words.enDefinition: Used to point out that one expression conveys the same idea as another in context.

examples.en: That's another way of saying we take turns using the room on different days.
examples.zh: 「那是另一种说法」，意思是我们分别在不同的日子轮流用这个房间。

examples.en: That's another way of saying the two groups meet in the same place first.
examples.zh: 「那是另一种说法」，意思是两组先在同一个地方碰面。

collocations: that's another way of saying it ends early
that's another way of saying we're taking turns
explain that's another way of saying it

words.enDefinition: Used to identify the most important detail within a longer explanation.

examples.en: The main thing is that nobody leaves without knowing which door to use tomorrow.
examples.zh: 「最重要的是」，每个人离开前都要知道明天走哪扇门。

examples.en: The main thing is to tell everyone where to put the chairs after practice.
examples.zh: 「最重要的是」，告诉大家练习结束后把椅子放在哪里。

collocations: the main thing is the timing
the main thing is that we all know
the main thing is to tell everyone

words.enDefinition: To give a simpler version by not including the smaller or less important points.

examples.en: I'll leave out the details for now and just give you the three main points.
examples.zh: 我先「略去细节」，只跟你讲三个要点。

examples.en: My neighbour chose to leave out the details until we had agreed where to start.
examples.zh: 在我们确定从哪里开始前，邻居选择先「略去细节」。

collocations: leave out the details for now
leave out the details of each step
choose to leave out the details

words.enDefinition: To review something with another person so that both of you understand it.

examples.en: We could go over it together after the others leave to check nothing is missing.
examples.zh: 其他人走后，我们可以「一起过一遍」，看看有没有遗漏。

examples.en: Could we go over it together before I explain the route to our visitors?
examples.zh: 我给访客说明路线前，我们能「一起过一遍」吗？

collocations: go over it together once more
offer to go over it together
go over it together from the start

words.enDefinition: Used to correct an interpretation that differs from what you intended to communicate.

examples.en: That's not what I meant when I suggested we leave the boxes by the door.
examples.zh: 我提议把箱子留在门边时，「不是那个意思」。

examples.en: That's not what I meant, so let's check the dates against the original message.
examples.zh: 「那不是我的意思」，我们对照原消息核查一下日期吧。

collocations: that's not what I meant at all
explain that's not what I meant
that's not what I meant by that

words.enDefinition: Used when correcting a word or detail you said incorrectly in the first place.

examples.en: I meant to say Thursday when we were discussing which day to move the chairs.
examples.zh: 我们讨论哪天搬椅子时，「我本来想说的是」周四。

examples.en: I meant to say upstairs because the spare tables have already been moved from here.
examples.zh: 「我本来想说的是」楼上，因为备用桌已经从这里搬走了。

collocations: I meant to say Thursday
I meant to say the other one
I meant to say downstairs

words.enDefinition: Used to explain the meaning you originally understood from someone's words or a message.

examples.en: I took it to mean we should wait outside until someone came with the keys.
examples.zh: 「我当时理解成」我们该在外面等，直到有人带钥匙过来。

examples.en: I took it to mean Thursday evening because the next line mentioned Friday morning separately.
examples.zh: 下一行单独提到周五上午，所以「我当时理解成」是周四晚上。

collocations: I took it to mean tomorrow
I took it to mean both groups
I took it to mean we should wait

words.enDefinition: Used to acknowledge that your interpretation may have been mistaken.

examples.en: I might have misunderstood the last point about sharing the shelf with the other flat.
examples.zh: 关于跟另一户共用架子的最后一点，「我可能理解错了」。

examples.en: I might have misunderstood what you meant when you said everyone could leave early.
examples.zh: 你说大家都能早点走时，「我可能理解错了」你的意思。

collocations: I might have misunderstood the last point
I might have misunderstood your message
I might have misunderstood what you meant

words.zhGloss: 转述或翻译时丢了些意思
words.enDefinition: Used to say that part of a meaning was not carried over when it was translated or retold.
acceptedZhAnswers: 转述或翻译时丢了些意思

examples.en: Something got lost in translation when the notice was shortened for the smaller poster.
examples.zh: 通知缩短印到小海报上时，「有些意思没能传达出来」。

examples.en: Something got lost in translation when we passed the plan along to the second group.
examples.zh: 我们把计划转述给第二个小组时，「漏掉了一些原意」。

collocations: something got lost in translation along the way
something got lost in translation between versions
say something got lost in translation

words.zhGloss: 我们把彼此的意思弄岔了
words.enDefinition: An informal way to say two people misunderstood each other or received conflicting messages.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们把彼此的意思弄岔了

examples.en: We got our wires crossed because you thought I was bringing the stand tonight.
examples.zh: 你以为我今晚会带架子过来，看来「我们把彼此的意思弄岔了」。

examples.en: I think we got our wires crossed about who was meeting the visitors at the door.
examples.zh: 我觉得关于谁去门口接访客，「我们把彼此的意思弄岔了」。

collocations: I think we got our wires crossed
we got our wires crossed about the date
explain how we got our wires crossed

words.enDefinition: Two possible interpretations of the same word, phrase, or other message.

examples.en: The phrase has two different meanings depending on which part of the map we're discussing.
examples.zh: 这句话有「两种不同的意思」，要看我们说的是地图上的哪一部分。

examples.en: We found two different meanings for the same abbreviation in our building's welcome guide.
examples.zh: 我们在楼里的欢迎指南里发现，同一个缩写有「两种不同的意思」。

collocations: have two different meanings
point out two different meanings
explain two different meanings

words.enDefinition: Used to say a new explanation is clearer or seems more logical than the earlier one.

examples.en: That makes more sense now that I know the cupboard is shared between two flats.
examples.zh: 现在我知道两家共用这个柜子，「这样就更说得通了」。

examples.en: That makes more sense if the second group arrives after we've put the tables away.
examples.zh: 如果第二组在我们收好桌子后才到，「这样就更说得通了」。

collocations: that makes more sense to me
that makes more sense now
say that makes more sense

words.expression: now I see what you mean
words.lemma: now i see what you mean
words.zhGloss: 现在我明白你的意思了
words.enDefinition: Used to show that additional information helped you understand the speaker's earlier point.
acceptedZhAnswers: 现在我明白你的意思了
acceptedEnVariants: now I see what you mean

examples.en: Now I see what you mean about putting all the signs at the same height.
examples.zh: 关于所有指示牌都放同一高度的事，「现在我明白你的意思了」。

examples.en: Now I see what you mean about folding the cloth before putting it away.
examples.zh: 关于把布叠好再收起来的事，「现在我明白你的意思了」。

collocations: now I see what you mean about the timing
now I see what you mean by that
say now I see what you mean
